text:
Maya: Heads-up — Legal asked for a "deletion proof" artifact for a DSAR yesterday that must cover derived embeddings/vectors. Our snapshot + backup + KMS rotation paths make it hard to prove deletion deterministically. Also need an RBAC exception so a privacy service account can delete cross-region snapshots. Any quick ideas?
Samir: Two immediate gaps I see: (1) durable proof for storage-level deletes (cache/GPU memory is transient), (2) immutable backups/snapshots that we can't immediately mutate. For (1) propose an erasure_receipt pattern: store {object_path, sha256, deletion_ts, request_id, key_version} and sign it with a signing-only key (KMS/HSM). We NEVER store plaintext. For (2) retention-exception workflow + manifest listing objects in affected backups. Also we'll need a scoped RBAC role for privacy-sa with only snapshot:delete and audit-write. Drafting PR.
Oliver: Legal will likely accept a signed hash + deletion tx id if it's auditable. We need chain-of-custody: request_id, operator, key_version, timestamp. Can KMS sign directly? Concern: could a rogue admin forge receipts?
Samir: Yes, Cloud KMS supports asymmetric signing. We'll use a signing-only key (no decrypt). Sign over a canonical string: sha256||"|"||path||"|"||ts||"|"||request_id||"|"||key_version. Store the signed receipt in AuditDB (immutable S3 with versioning + restricted ACL). Admins can't edit AuditDB. Include key_version in receipt so verification is possible.
Sarah (Legal): That sounds reasonable. For backups that are WORM or vendor-managed snapshots, Legal needs a retention-exception notice and expected expiry timeline. We'll need a small playbook: retention-exception request, approver, and communications to data subject if deletion is delayed. Redaction plans for DR copies are acceptable where full delete isn't feasible immediately.
Maya: Edge case: what if KMS rotation is in-flight and the signing key is unavailable when a DSAR arrives? We can't block users indefinitely. Options?
Samir: Fallbacks: (A) maintain a rotating buffer of signing keys (keep last N keys able to sign) so rotation doesn't block us, or (B) mark the DSAR as "pending" and create an immutable tombstone record in AuditDB with request_id, paths, and hashes. Once KMS finishes, we issue the signed receipt that references that tombstone. Tombstones must be append-only and tamper-evident (S3 versioning + restricted writes).
deploy-bot: :warning: KMS rotation job started for keystore/signing-key at 3120001200 — any DSAR processed between 3120001200 and 3120001400 may be unsigned. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-rotation
Oliver: Legal question: is a "pending" tombstone + signed follow-up acceptable? We also need confirmation that the data subject was notified with the timeline.
Sarah (Legal): Pending is acceptable if we (1) notify the user immediately with expected timeframe, (2) include the technical reason (eg. key rotation), and (3) follow up with a signed receipt when available. Also capture retention-exception metadata: approver, expiry, justification.
Maya: I'll open PR for RBAC role `privacy-erasure-sa` with minimal scope and another PR for audit schema changes. Samir, can you draft the tombstone + signing flow and a verification snippet?
Samir: Yep. I'll add the flow + tests. Example receipt payload we'll sign:```json
{
  "request_id":"req_20260321_01",
  "objects":["s3://redwood-eu/embeddings/abc123"],
  "sha256":"b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184",
  "deletion_ts":"2026-03-21T15:05:00Z",
  "key_version":"v20260321-3"
}```Signed bytes = sign(canonicalize(payload)). Storing signature and payload in AuditDB. PRs: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9876 (rbac) & https://github.com/redwood/platform/pull/2202 (audit-schema).
Oliver: Also update the incident playbook: when a vulnerability triage requires forensic hold, the DSAR deletion must be paused and a legal_hold record linked to the request_id. That needs a clear triage + sign-off path.
Maya: Good call. Action items: I will schedule a 30m sync after standup to triage RBAC+audit work. Samir will draft tombstone/signing flow and add tests. Legal will prepare the retention-exception template.
Samir: On it, will ping when drafts are ready.
Maya: Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source of truth. :thumbsup:
